collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Old villagers who feel overlooked start their own evening circle: keep it to themselves, or invite the young.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) and a few other old villagers have started meeting every evening by the old canoe house, because at the main fire nobody listens to them anymore. They tell stories, play the stone game and complain about the young. Some young people have noticed. What should the elders do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The elders' circle stays theirs. It is the liveliest place in the village after dark. The young people start sneaking close to listen to the stories. The elders pretend not to notice.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The elders invite anyone who wants to come and listen. A few young people come, then more. The stories get longer and better. The complaining about the young continues, now with the young laughing along.
